implementation_summary: Token verification now requires firebase.sign_in_provider === 'google.com' and refuses with the same fixed error otherwise. Added exported allows(grant, needed) in helper-access.ts as the single permission check, where edit and export include view. HelperAccess.refusal uses it. It is reachable via the helpers/index.ts export-star.

tests_executed.name: helper token, session, access and audit-helpers routes

tests_proposed: In audit-store.ts tests (BE-602): a grant with permissions ['edit'] or ['export'] must pass mayUseAudit for a view row.
evidence: helper-token.test.ts: 'accepts only the google.com sign-in provider' covers google.com accepted; password, github.com, empty, null and missing firebase refused.
audit-helpers-routes.test.ts: a password-provider token gets 401 ERR_SIGN_IN_FAILED.
helper-access.test.ts: allows() covers edit and export including view, and view not allowing edit.
risks: Firebase tokens without the firebase.sign_in_provider claim are now refused. Real Google sign-in tokens carry it.
Until audit-store.ts adopts allows(), the dispatch path (which expands view) and the route handlers (which read stored permissions as-is) still disagree.
handoff: BE-602 / audit-store.ts: import { allows, grantedPermissions } from './helpers/index.js' (path relative to routes/). In grantedAuditIds and mayUseAudit (~line 62), do not read grant.permissions directly. Replace permission checks with allows(grant, needed), for example mayUseAudit => grant !== null && allows(grant, 'view'), and for edit or export rows allows(grant, 'edit') or allows(grant, 'export'). grantedAuditIds should filter grants with allows(g, 'view'). allows takes any object with a permissions array, so a HelperGrant works directly.
